LESSON: DATA PRESENTATION AND INTERPRETATION

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: GRADE
Strand: DATA HANDLING AND PROBABILITY
Topic 5.1: DATA PRESENTATION AND INTERPRETATION
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers DATA PRESENTATION AND INTERPRETATION, part of DATA HANDLING AND PROBABILITY in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 8 GRADE.

Key inquiry question: Why is data presentation important? 2. How do we determine the mean of data?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on DATA PRESENTATION AND INTERPRETATION together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
;

● Communication and collaboration: Writing, observing, and signing; as learners discuss and represent data in line graphs in

groups.

● Critical thinking and problem solving imagines different situations and generates ideas; as the learner discuss and interpret

Bar graphs

● Self-efficacy: Keep trying when something goes wrong; as the learner collects data from their own experiences, for

example size of shoes, height or test scores and draws line and bar graphs from the data.

Values:
● Love: As the learner carries out different activities that involve getting the median position in groups harmoniously. For

example, where possible learners use the hand to identify the middle finger in reference to the position.

● Respect: As the learner discusses and represents data in line graphs in groups.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Socio-Economic and Environmental Issues: Environmental education; as learners collect data from the immediate

environment or experiences, for example size of shoes, height, or test scores.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner is able to relate the skill of presenting data using graphs to representing data using charts and graphs in Social

Studies.
